candidate.answerReason: Under the standard constant-speed model with equal walking pace in both trials, choosing a length of 120 units gives walking speed 2, combined speed 5, and escalator speed 3 units per second. The ride takes 120/3 = 40 seconds.

methods.label: Choose convenient distance units
methods.explanation:
Use the usual model that Clea keeps the same constant walking pace relative to the steps in both trials and that the operating escalator moves at a constant speed.

Choose the unit of length so that the escalator is \(120\) units long. This makes both observed speeds whole numbers. With the escalator stopped, Clea's walking speed is
\[
120\div60=2
\]
units per second. With it operating, her speed relative to the building is \(120\div24=5\) units per second.

Walking and the escalator both carry her downward, so their speeds add. The escalator's own speed is therefore \(5-2=3\) units per second. When Clea stands still on it, her travel time is
\[
120\div3=40
\]
seconds. The answer is \(\boxed{40}\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Convenient length units reduce the rate calculation to whole-number division and subtraction.

candidate.annotationRationale: The route-neutral target is the relationship between distance, speed, and time, covered by cnm_p111. Subtracting the walking contribution uses inverse arithmetic relationships, and the selected units use integer division. Meeting and catching-up criteria are not required by this method.
limitations: The result uses the standard implicit model of constant escalator speed and the same walking speed relative to the steps in both trials.

review.mathematicalCheck: Under the explicitly stated constant-speed model, a length of 120 units gives walking and combined speeds of 2 and 5 units per second. The escalator speed is 3, so standing takes 120/3=40 seconds. Choosing units introduces no special physical length.
review.levelCheck: Convenient units reduce the reasoning to elementary division, speed addition, and subtraction.
